es.summary: La creatinina sérica es un producto de desecho muscular que se elimina por los riñones y sirve para evaluar la función renal.
key_points: Rango normal adulto: 0.5‑1.0 mg/dL mujeres, 0.7‑1.2 mg/dL hombres (varía por laboratorio).
Elevaciones indican posible insuficiencia renal aguda o crónica.
La relación BUN/creatinina ≈ 20:1 ayuda a diferenciar causas prerrenales vs. renales.
Factores que alteran la creatinina: masa muscular, dieta rica en carne roja, hidratación y medicamentos nefrotóxicos.

normal_values: Valores pueden variar según edad y método del laboratorio
high_values: Uso de fármacos nefrotóxicos (ej. aminoglucósidos, AINEs)
Síntomas: oliguria, edema, fatiga, náuseas, confusión
specimen: Muestra de suero o plasma; tubo SST con gel separador
No requiere ayuno, pero se prefiere muestra matutina
Evitar hemólisis; mezclar suavemente el tubo
En caso de prueba de creatinina urinaria, recolectar 24 h completa
nursing_care: Monitorear creatinina y BUN cada 24‑48 h según orden médica
Evaluar gasto urinario, color y presencia de edema
Revisar medicamentos nefrotóxicos y ajustar dosis renal
Educar al paciente sobre hidratación adecuada y dieta balanceada
Reportar valores fuera de rango al médico inmediatamente

outcomes: Función renal: creatinina sérica dentro del rango normal para su sexo y edad
Balance hídrico: ingesta y salida de líquidos equilibradas (±10 % de la necesidad estimada)

interventions.action: Obtener y registrar la creatinina sérica y BUN según orden médica.
interventions.rationale: Permite evaluar la función renal y detectar cambios tempranos.

interventions.action: Monitorear el gasto urinario cada 2 h y reportar disminuciones <0.5 mL/kg/h.
interventions.rationale: La oliguria es un signo precoz de perfusión renal comprometida.

interventions.action: Revisar la lista de medicamentos y notificar al médico si hay fármacos nefrotóxicos.
interventions.rationale: Reducir la exposición a agentes que pueden empeorar la función renal.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de una hidratación adecuada (≈30 mL/kg/día).
interventions.rationale: Mantener el volumen intravascular ayuda a preservar la perfusión renal.

interventions.action: Controlar signos de sobrecarga de líquidos: edema, presión arterial alta, crepitantes.
interventions.rationale: La sobrecarga puede empeorar la perfusión renal y la función cardíaca.

en.summary: Serum creatinine is a muscular waste product eliminated by the kidneys and is used to assess renal function.
key_points: Normal adult range: 0.5‑1.0 mg/dL women, 0.7‑1.2 mg/dL men (varies by laboratory).
Elevations suggest possible acute or chronic renal failure.
The BUN/creatinine ratio ≈ 20:1 helps differentiate prerenal vs. renal causes.
Factors that alter creatinine: muscle mass, high red‑meat diet, hydration, nephrotoxic medications.

normal_values: Values may vary with age and laboratory method
high_values: Use of nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., aminoglycosides, NSAIDs)
Symptoms: oliguria, edema, fatigue, nausea, confusion
specimen: Serum or plasma sample; SST tube with gel separator
No fasting required, but morning sample preferred
For urinary creatinine test, collect a complete 24‑hour sample
nursing_care: Monitor serum creatinine and BUN every 24‑48 h per order
Assess urine output, color, and presence of edema
Review nephrotoxic medications and adjust renal dosing
Educate patient on adequate hydration and balanced diet
Report out‑of‑range values to the physician immediately

outcomes: Renal function: serum creatinine within normal range for sex and age
Fluid balance: intake and output balanced (±10 % of estimated need)

interventions.action: Obtain and record serum creatinine and BUN per order.
interventions.rationale: Allows assessment of renal function and early detection of changes.

interventions.action: Monitor urine output every 2 h and report decreases <0.5 mL/kg/h.
interventions.rationale: Oliguria is an early sign of compromised renal perfusion.

interventions.action: Review medication list and notify physician if nephrotoxic drugs are present.
interventions.rationale: Reduce exposure to agents that may worsen renal function.

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of adequate hydration (≈30 mL/kg/day).
interventions.rationale: Maintaining intravascular volume helps preserve renal perfusion.

interventions.action: Monitor for signs of fluid overload: edema, high blood pressure, crackles.
interventions.rationale: Overload can worsen renal perfusion and cardiac function.

summary.0.quote: Creatinine Serum creatinine is the waste product of muscle tissue metabolism. It is completely cleared by the kidneys, which means that creatinine levels can be used to assess kidney function.

sections.normal_values.2.quote: In general, the normal BUN range is 10 to 20 mg/dL, but normal ranges vary depending on the reference range used by the laboratory and the patient’s age.

sections.high_values.0.quote: An eGFR value less than 60 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 for 3 consecutive months indicates chronic renal disease, and an eGFR value less than 15 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 indicates kidney failure or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) .

sections.specimen.3.quote: Serum creatinine and urine creatinine can be compared to estimate renal function; however, the relationship between the two values changes as the GFR falls, and this comparison requires collecting urine over 24 hours as directed.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Maintain adequate intake of fluids as prescribed by their health care provider.
